segments.t: At home, Nastya tells Kostya to close his eyes and open his mouth so she can swab his cheek for the DNA test. Back at the hotel, Mikhail warns Viktor Petrovich that Patrick Malouda is arriving—only to discover that someone stole Barinov's wheelchair!
Костик, закрой глаза и открой рот.
Эй, стой на месте сейчас же!
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Костик, закрой глаза и открой рот.
'Kostik, close your eyes and open your mouth.' Mentioning the eyes during the talk, Nastya leans on "glaza" ("eyes", a form of "glaz") to give the remark its edge.
'Why should I open my mouth right now?' Bringing up his mouth during the talk, Barinov puts the question word "zachem" right at the start so Nastya hears the focus immediately.
'It is necessary, come on, open up quickly.' Nastya fires back lightly hearing Barinov, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'Nastya, is this some kind of joke?' Underscoring the joke beside Nastya, Barinov leans on "shutka" ("joke, prank") to give the whole sentence its punch.
'Vitya, the inspector already called me.' Bringing up the inspector in front of Barinov, Mikhail brings in "inspektor" ("inspector") to make the meaning unmistakable.
'He will be here very soon.' Mikhail reacts openly toward Barinov, shifting the mood of the conversation in a single beat.
'So come on, get the wheelchair ready.' Turning to the wheelchair during the talk, Mikhail brings in "kolyasku" ("wheelchair", from "kolyaska") as the key Russian word here.
'Wait, where is my wheelchair?' Touching on his wheelchair in front of Mikhail, Barinov puts the question word "gde" right at the start so Mikhail hears the focus immediately.
'How could you lose the wheelchair?' Mikhail challenges bluntly why things suddenly took this turn between them.
Эй, стой на месте сейчас же!
'Hey, stop right there this instant!' Bringing up the place beside Mikhail, Barinov chooses "meste" ("place", from the root "mesto") so Mikhail hears the exact meaning.
'Where are you riding off to on it?' Turning openly on the spot, Barinov puts the question word "kuda" right at the start so Mikhail hears the focus immediately.
'Well, what are you doing over there?' Mikhail prompts briskly before Barinov can change the subject.
Костик, закрой глаза и открой рот.
Эй, стой на месте сейчас же!
With the wheelchair rolling down the street and the Michelin inspector minutes away, Senya and Fedya race out to find a replacement. See you next time!
